note: Check DNS is a zero-config validation add-on: hook_form_user_register_form_alter() appends check_dns_user_register_validate to the core user_register_form #validate, which calls check_dns.service (Drupal\check_dns\CheckDnsService). validateEmail() runs FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL then validateHost(), which returns dns_check_record()/checkdnsrr() (default MX) for the domain. No settings form (configure=null), no permissions, no config, no Drush, no plugins. Medium cases interrogate the live service (real DNS works in this container: drupal.org -> TRUE, *.invalid -> FALSE). Hard cases toggle the module's enabled state and verify the registration form's validate handler is wired.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module check_dns blocks user registration when the email's domain looks fake. Technically, how does it decide a domain is invalid? Name the PHP function it ultimately calls and the default DNS record type checked.
evals.expected_output: The check_dns.service (CheckDnsService) validateEmail() first runs FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL, then takes the domain after '@' and calls validateHost(), which returns dns_check_record($host) -- an alias of PHP's checkdnsrr(), whose default record type is MX. If the domain has no such DNS record the service returns FALSE.

evals.prompt: I enabled check_dns but can't find a settings page. Which form does it hook into to validate the email domain, and what service id can I call from my own code to run the same check?
evals.expected_output: There is no settings page (configure=null). check_dns_form_user_register_form_alter() adds check_dns_user_register_validate to the core user registration form (user_register_form) #validate array. From code you call \Drupal::service('check_dns.service')->validateEmail($mail) (or ->validateHost($host)).

evals.prompt: Does check_dns verify that a specific email mailbox exists, or only something about the domain? And what error does a user see when the check fails at registration?
evals.expected_output: It only checks that the email's DOMAIN has a DNS record; it does not verify the individual mailbox exists. On failure the registration form sets an error on the mail field: 'Your email domain is not recognised. Please enter a valid email id.'

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use check_dns to determine whether the email address 'user@drupal.org' would be accepted as a valid registration email. Inspect the running site (do not guess) and state the result.
evals.expected_output: Valid/accepted. Running \Drupal::service('check_dns.service')->validateEmail('user@drupal.org') on the live site returns TRUE because drupal.org has a resolvable DNS/MX record.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use check_dns's host validation to determine whether the domain 'no-such-domain-xyz123abc.invalid' has a usable DNS record. Inspect the running site and state whether it passes or fails the check.
evals.expected_output: Fails. \Drupal::service('check_dns.service')->validateHost('no-such-domain-xyz123abc.invalid') returns FALSE on the live site because the reserved .invalid domain has no DNS record.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the check_dns module is currently uninstalled, so nothing stops signups that use email addresses at non-existent domains. Enable check_dns so that its email-domain check is wired onto the user registration form. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Run `drush en check_dns -y`. After this, hook_form_user_register_form_alter() attaches check_dns_user_register_validate to the user_register_form #validate, so registrations with a non-resolving email domain are rejected by check_dns.service.

evals.prompt: Lots of spam accounts are signing up on my Drupal site using fake email addresses whose domains don't even exist. There's a module already downloaded for this called 'Check DNS'. Please switch it on so the signup form refuses those bogus email domains.
evals.expected_output: Enable the check_dns module (e.g. `drush en check_dns -y`). Once enabled it adds a validation handler to the registration form that rejects email addresses whose domain has no DNS record.
